divergence.summary: The model does not reproduce this death, and the reason is a stated mechanic difference worth measuring before Night 6.
divergence.modelSays: minus3-frame-light.mjs --census reports minBox 0.6525 on Night 5 across 3000 seeds: the model never lets the music box approach empty on this schedule, so it cannot produce a Puppet kill. Its 364/3000 losses are all inside-office, spread across 1..5 AM.
divergence.deviceSaw: two attempts died within 2.4 s of each other (368.97 s and 366.61 s) after a desync at ~5 AM, to two different animatronics (Puppet, then Mangle). The common cause is the desync and the box failure, not the animatronic.
divergence.mechanism: plant-model.js:306 drops every non-mask touch while the mask surface owns input (maskOn || maskAnim > 0), and the schedule's mask and monitor presses are toggles. A blackout that holds the masked state past the schedule's mask-off tap therefore eats the following monitor/wind/camera presses and can invert the schedule's mask/monitor phase for the rest of the night, which is what winding stopping looks like.
divergence.whereTheModelDiffers: startBlackout records masked = maskFullyOn and only requires the mask to have been fully on before maskGraceFrames; nothing re-checks that it is still on when BLACKOUT_FRAMES (5 s) expires. The model therefore lets the schedule pull the mask off mid-blackout and stay in phase. Whether the device holds the mask for the full blackout is the measurement that would settle it.
divergence.openQuestion: measure, from the retained video, how long the masked state actually persists across a device blackout versus the 5 s BLACKOUT_FRAMES and the schedule's 5.18 s mask window, and whether any scheduled press between them was dropped
divergence.modelCannotAttribute: all 364/3000 Night 5 model losses on this schedule are 'Toy Bonnie completed the sourced 40-frame marker-123 attack'. The model produces no Puppet and no Mangle office death here, so its 2636/3000 (87.9%) is both optimistic and mis-attributed for this route on device.
divergence.eatenCycleCost: modelled by dropping every scheduled press for N consecutive clear cycles at 5 AM (600 seeds): 0 cycles 527/600 with minBox 0.652; 1 cycle 472/600 with minBox 0.160; 2 cycles 71/600 with minBox 0.000 and 371 puppet deaths; 3 cycles 0/600 with 482 puppet deaths. One eaten cycle costs almost the whole box margin and two empty it, which reproduces the device death. Extending the wind (windAtMs 5400, windMs 3600) raises the floor only 0.160 -> 0.176 and changes no win count, so this is not tunable by winding.

the save cursor stands at Night 5; a death does not roll it back

puppetStun.claim: An empty music box is survivable: holding the camera light while viewing CAM 11 blocks the Puppet's escape rolls outright.
puppetStun.source: plant-model.js, the g494/g495 branch: while box <= 0 and the Puppet has not escaped, each one-second roll is skipped entirely when camLightOn && viewing === BOX_CAM. It is a block, not a reduced chance.
puppetStun.observedOnDevice: night5-r2: after the box failed, the schedule's CAM 11 flashes held the Marionette for the rest of the run; Mangle, not the Puppet, ended it (operator, live).
puppetStun.whyNotJustHoldTheLight: refuted in the model before spending a device run: holding the light through the 3.2 s wind phase gives 0/3000 on Nights 5 and 6, minPower 0, with 2942/3000 Night 5 deaths to foxy -- pressing the light after Foxy has locked on is itself a kill (plant-model.js:354), and the added duty exhausts the flashlight.
puppetStun.whatItIsWorth: a targeted emergency fallback rather than a schedule change: camp CAM 11 lit only once the box is actually empty. That requires observing the box level, so it is an argument for a box-level read in the Cue Helper, not something an open-loop schedule can spend.

killerCensus.claim: Every Night 5 death on the Minus 3 route was a Toy or the box; not one Withered.
killerCensus.frames: killer frames were recovered from each run's retained screenrecord, not from the 5 s screencap cadence, which missed every jumpscare. r3-vent additionally shows Balloon Boy's 'BALLOONS!' sign at the extreme left of the Foxy jumpscare: BB was inside the office, and plant-model.js gates anyOfficeLightHeld and hallLightOn on !bb.inside, so every hall flash was dead and Foxy's approach timer never reset.
killerCensus.conclusion: This is the Minus 3 route's documented boundary arriving one night earlier than expected. The route parks the CAM 08 marker to hold the three Withereds and leaves the Toys live, which is safe while Toy AI is 1-2 on Nights 3-5 and is not safe here. The model cannot see it: all 364/3000 of its Night 5 losses are Toy Bonnie, an animatronic that killed us zero times on device.

minusToysOnNight5.actuatorHypothesis: The strategy is byte-identical to the authoritative queue -- verified press for press against minus-toys-plan schedule() -- and the model gates it 3000/3000, so a 2/2 device failure at 12 AM had to be actuator-side. Two contact-level facts explain it: a 33 ms contact is long enough to register as a UI tap but not to hold the hall light (the repo's own 17 ms probe landed 3/3 camera sweeps while the independent light-effect gate accepted 0/3), and a flash scheduled 300 ms after the mask-off tap sits only ~56 ms clear of the 244 ms MASK_ANIM_OFF window, during which plant-model.js drops every non-mask touch.

unenforcedConstraint.finding: The plan compiler does not enforce mask-animation clearance. MASK_ANIM_OFF is referenced in 16 files including minus-3-plan.mjs, whose author left explicit room for it, but zero times in tools/device/artifact-commands.mjs or tools/device/bundle.mjs -- the compiler and the validator.
unenforcedConstraint.consequence: The emitted minus-toys loop is [9200 tap mask 33][9500 hall 33][10100 tap monitor 33]: a 300 ms gap against a 244 ms animation, 56 ms of margin, checked by nothing. A plan that schedules a press into the window the engine drops should fail to build, not fail on the phone.
unenforcedConstraint.proposedRule: compileCycle should track the mask-off press time and refuse any non-mask action that begins within MASK_ANIM_OFF of it, the same way it already refuses a camdrop with the monitor down.

minusToysOnNight5.remaining: Both routes now fail on Night 5 for the same reason: an eaten input inverts a toggle and the mask/monitor phase never recovers. Minus 3 lost the box to it; Minus Toys lost the mask to it. Open-loop cannot self-correct, so the next real step is state-aware actuation, not more knobs.

compilerAcceptsInvalidInteraction.finding: tools/device/artifact-commands.mjs compileCycle declares a monitor precondition for a plain tap/hold row only when the control is a camera or wind: `const needsUp = camera(row.control) || control === 'wind'`. A raw `hold ventl` therefore declares no precondition and is compiled unguarded, even though plant-model.js gates every vent light on hallView (`monitor !== MON_UP`).
compilerAcceptsInvalidInteraction.contrast: The precondition system exists and is used: mask throws 'mask toggle requires monitor down', camdrop throws 'camdrop requires monitor up', and the `read` compound throws 'vent read requires monitor down'. The vent controls are guarded only in that compound, not as raw holds.
compilerAcceptsInvalidInteraction.observedOnDevice: Operator, watching with show_touches during toys-n5-vent350: taps carrying the left vent light coordinate land inside the monitor and hit the camera flash instead. The emitted minus-toys loop raises the monitor at 10100 and presses ventl at 10400, so every vent press in the plan happens with the monitor up.

modelDependsOnIt.note: The model scores the invalid arrangement far higher because press('ventL') sets ventLightL, which feeds anyOfficeLightHeld -- and that getter does NOT require hallView, unlike every ventLightOn getter. So the simulator credits an office-light hold that the device cannot produce with the monitor up. Removing the row entirely costs 3000/3000 -> 1046/3000, so it is load-bearing, not decorative.

compilerAcceptsInvalidInteraction.consequence: Enforcing the rule would refuse the currently shipped minus-toys plan, which is the device-proven nights 1-2 winner. The plan needs re-deriving under the constraint, not just re-timing, because the legal arrangements score far worse in the model. Flagged for Pedro; not changed by the agent.
compilerAcceptsInvalidInteraction.RETRACTED: See RETRACTION_ventPress: ventl is the camera-feed light by design; this entry's premise is wrong.

startDelayCensus.note: an earlier 1000-seed version of this table was recorded in commit a8260aa and is superseded here
startDelayCensus.reading: The lane's measured 26-30 s office-to-schedule-start latency is harmless on Night 1, marginal on Night 2 and fatal on Night 5. Night 2's device win therefore cleared a night the model gives 12.7% at that latency. With the latency removed the route is 3000/3000 on all three.

laneLatencyFixed.cause: apps/device/src/adb-device-local-executor.js appendWrites emitted one shell command per HID stream line -- `printf '%s\n' <line> >> file` for each of several hundred lines across prefix, remainder and rearm -- so the device script spent roughly 25 s opening, appending to and closing files before it registered /system/bin/hid at all.
laneLatencyFixed.foundBy: startup phase anchors added to the executor (hid.execute-entered, hid.shell-spawned, hid.night-go). Two earlier fixes each claimed to remove this latency without measuring it; the anchors showed the schedule spawning 8.7 s BEFORE the office and still not starting for another 23 s, which ruled out the spawn point and pointed at the script itself.
laneLatencyFixed.fix: one printf per file; `printf '%s\n' a b c` reuses its format for every argument
laneLatencyFixed.deviceEffect: minus-toys Night 5 went from a box exhausted before the schedule began (operator: 'nope, box exhausted') to 283.8 s survived, the route's best by a wide margin over 171.3 s. Still not a win.
laneLatencyFixed.remainingGap: The model gives minus-toys Night 5 3000/3000 at zero latency but the device reached 68% of the night, which is consistent with the model's own 'without ventl' score of 1046/3000: the emitted vent press fires with the monitor up and lands on the camera flash, so the device is effectively running the variant the model scores at 35%. That is the compiler gap already recorded here.
laneLatencyFixed.killer: Balloon Boy (operator, live). The operator noted the run defended blackouts without a single forced-down monitor or missed mask window, which is structural rather than lucky: startBlackout records masked = maskFullyOn at the instant the encounter begins, and the cycle holds the mask ~4.8 s of every 10 s in fixed phase, so a large share of encounters find the mask already up and need no reaction. BB is the one threat the mask does not answer -- bb.inside kills every office light -- and his counter is the vent light, which is the press this plan fires with the monitor up. The best run therefore died to exactly the animatronic the broken press exists to stop.

monitorRaiseNotPricedForDevice.question: is the monitor-up animation priced correctly? (operator, 2026-09-09)
monitorRaiseNotPricedForDevice.modelSide: MONITOR_ANIM_UP is 12 engine frames, commented 0.204 s, while C.FPS is 60 -- so the millisecond figure depends on an assumed frame rate. tools/sourcetest.mjs constrains it only relatively (MONITOR_ANIM_DOWN > MONITOR_ANIM_UP); there is no absolute assertion anywhere in the green lane.
monitorRaiseNotPricedForDevice.profileSide: apps/device/profiles/hid-mediaprojection.json calibrations['actuator-timing'] is the string 'hid-100ms-candidate-unqualified-v1'. No measured monitor-raise readiness exists, and the entry names itself unqualified.
monitorRaiseNotPricedForDevice.deviceBracket: a wind hold at raise+200 ms (5500, the earliest my new compiler gate allows, derived from the model constant) MISSED: the operator saw the wind taps not land and the run died to the Marionette at 44.3 s, against 195-369 s for the same schedule with the wind at raise+500 ms (5800). Earlier, raise+100 ms (5400) also missed. So device readiness is bracketed in (200 ms, 500 ms] after the press, and 200 ms is not it.
monitorRaiseNotPricedForDevice.likelyMechanism: the raise plausibly starts on RELEASE of the 33 ms tap rather than the press, putting the animation at [5333, 5533] and a 5500 press inside it. Untested.
monitorRaiseNotPricedForDevice.consequenceForTheGate: the animation-clearance rule I landed uses the model constant as the deadline, so it permits exactly the schedule that failed. It is still worth having -- it refuses the worse 5400 case -- but its threshold must become a measured readiness plus a jitter margin, which is what tools/device/recipe.mjs already does for Minus 7 via RAISE_JITTER_MARGIN_MS and RAISE_MARGIN_MS. Until measured, no plan may shave this gap.
monitorRaiseNotPricedForDevice.howToMeasure: tools/device/hid-monitorraise-probe.mjs, tools/device/monitorraise-watch.py and tools/device/monitor-calibrate.py exist for this; the output belongs in the profile's actuator-timing calibration, replacing the unqualified candidate string.

RETRACTION_ventPress.retracts: compilerAcceptsInvalidInteraction and the related claims in plans/PROGRESS.md and commits 0eb0280 and 60cb462, which said the emitted minus-toys plan presses an office vent light with the monitor up, that the press is inert on device, and that the model wrongly credits it.
RETRACTION_ventPress.whatIsActuallyTrue: `ventl` in minus-toys-plan.mjs is the CAMERA-FEED light, deliberately. actionFor maps `ventl` -> the sim action `light` (tools/device/minus-toys-plan.mjs:203), and the knobs document it as 'ventl (camera-feed light) glitch-stun refresh, right after the raise' and 'ventl (CAM 09 feed light) re-flash'. The row is named for the profile control whose coordinate coincides with the camera feed light. The sim receives press('light') with the monitor up, which is camLightOn -- the camera flash -- so the model and the device agree. The operator's observation that taps carrying the left-vent coordinate land inside the monitor and hit the cam flash is the plan working as intended, not a defect.
consequences: the 3000/3000 night-5 gate is not built on a phantom effect; it rests on the camera-feed glitch-stun
the compiler rule drafted to refuse 'vent light with monitor up' would have refused an intentional press; it was never landed and must not be, at least not in that form
the 3000/3000 -> 1046/3000 figure came from deleting the row entirely, which removes a real camera-flash stun; it is not the cost of the press being inert

the anyOfficeLightHeld fix remains correct on its own terms -- the dump requires viewing = 0 for g301/g303/g320 -- but it does not touch these plans, because they never emit a ventL action at all. sourcetest stays 203/203 and the night-5 gate stays 3000/3000 with it applied
RETRACTION_ventPress.howItWasCaught: printing the distinct sim actions in the emitted queue: ['monitor','cam:11','cam:9','wind','light','mask'] -- no vent action exists in it.
